The applicant’s revised plan gives 400 MW final IT load across ten buildings and roughly 500–600 MW total demand, replacing the 153 MW tracker claim.

references.title: Data Center Development — Shawnee County
Compass Datacenters — Revised Operations Plan
ArcGIS — SW85thStreet/SWBurlingameRoad vicinity

patch.longFormSummary:
• The filing distinguishes 607.6 acres in its opening narrative from 611.67 acres in its site calculation; this discrepancy remains open. The plan describes air-cooled/closed-loop cooling, not a measured daily water reading. The old$1.1 B cost is unsupported.
  • Map marker is the approximate SW 85 th/Burlingame intersection at 38.91328,-95.73393, near the proposed tract, not a surveyed project center or boundary. Final permits and subsequent review restrictions remain to be checked.
  • Timeline: June 1,2028 remains an unverified legacy COD. An application-completeness decision is not construction or operating approval.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy June 2028 COD; county completeness determination is not an approved schedule.
patch.address: SW77th–SW85th Street/Burlingame Road vicinity, unincorporated Shawnee County, Kansas (approximate intersection marker)

power.note: Full-buildout critical IT design; total demand estimated 500–600 MW, not energized.

datacenter.cooling: Proposed air-cooled and liquid closed-loop cooling
datacenter.note: Ten single-story 267000 sqft buildings planned.607.6 vs 611.67 acre discrepancy unresolved. No daily water reading.

gaps: Verify current moratorium/review restrictions and permit outcome, exact footprint/acreage, phased power service, budget and COD; marker is only a vicinity intersection.

patch.title: Deep Atomic INL: Proposed Nuclear/AI Campus;60 MWe Reactor Design Is Not IT Load
patch.description: Deep Atomic and partners submitted an INL campus proposal in late 2025. The reported MK 60 concept supplies 60 MW electrical and 60 MW cooling, with 200 MW thermal output. Those are reactor-design quantities, not verified operating data-center IT demand or an approved$800 M campus.

references.title: SMR developer Deep Atomic proposes nuclear-powered AI data center at Idaho National Lab

patch.longFormSummary:
• The consortium proposes starting computing on grid/geothermal/solar while reactor design certification and commissioning proceed. It is a proposal, not DOE selection or nuclear operating authorization.
  • The old 60 MW usage row, closed-loop water claims, scaled consumption and$800 M budget are unverified and cleared. The developer’s current.io site was inaccessible; no generic SMR image is represented as a built INL campus.
  • Timeline: December 31,2028 remains an unverified legacy COD. The 24–36 month proposal timetable is conditional and lacks an approved trigger.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy December 2028 COD; conditional 24–36 month concept is not an approved INL schedule.

gaps: Verify DOE proposal outcome, exact site/authorization, reactor vsIT capacity, approved schedule, budget and cooling/water design; operator site inaccessible.
Could not verify the search-indexed Deep Atomic entry in the downloaded Idaho RFI paper; it was not used as project evidence.

patch.title: Digi Power X Columbiana:15 MW First Phase Targets December 15,2026;40 MW by Q1 2027
patch.description: Digi Power X’s May 8,2026 filing identifies a Cerebras colocation agreement:15 MW first-phase IT targeted ready December 15,2026, and 40 MW total by end-Q1 2027, with the additional 25 MW subject to financing. The old 55 MW IT/$450 M campus claims are not established.

references.title: Digi Power X — Form8-K filedMay8,2026
Digi Power X Signs AI Colocation Agreement with Leading AI Compute Company for40MW Data Center in Columbiana, Alabama

patch.longFormSummary:
• The$1.1 B initial ten-year service contract is revenue, not construction cost.40 MW is total planned IT;15 MW is the first phase, not 55 MW of critical load.
  • The former 15000 gal/day value labelled published could not be substantiated in the opened filing or current operator release; it is removed with unverified area and dependent energy. The release API is blocked, so the filed exhibit supplies evidence.
  • Timeline: December 15,2026 is the contractual first-phase target, not confirmed delivery. The 40 MW completion target is end-Q1 2027 and financing-dependent.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Contractual Phase 1 ready-for-service target in May 2026 filing; remains estimated pending delivery.

power.note: Planned total IT after two phases; first 15 MW target Dec 15,2026, incremental 25 MW financing-dependent.

gaps: Verify present construction/delivery, phase2 financing, site construction budget, actual water demand and exact parcel; service revenue is not capex.

patch.title: Rowan Bauxite I:Substantial Completion in 2025; Financing Is Not Campus Cost
patch.description: Rowan’s portfolio states Bauxite I reached substantial completion in 2025. Its January 2025 release announced$975 M construction financing, not a$1.2 B campus price. DCD reports 300 MW and four single-story buildings; the old 150 MW and future 2026 opening are unsupported.

references.title: Bauxite1,2,3 — Rowan Digital Infrastructure
Quinbrook’s Rowan Digital Infrastructure Secures $975 Million Financing for Hyperscale Campus in Maryland
Rowan secures $1.2bn for Maryland data center campus build-out

patch.longFormSummary:
• Reported Bauxite I floor area is 777150 sqft across four buildings. Combined I–III portfolio area/power is a different scope; old 120 ac and scaled water/energy claims are cleared.
  • Substantial completion is not proof that all 300 MW are energized or occupied. The operator’s financing and whole-portfolio capacity must not be mistaken for standalone operating cost/load.
  • Timeline: January 1,2025 is year-only precision for substantial completion, not a verified first-service day.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Operator reports substantial completion in 2025; year placeholder, not full energization/occupancy date.

power.note: Reported planned Bauxite I campus capacity, not verified energized IT load.

datacenter.note: Reported Bauxite I scope; whole I–III portfolio must not be apportioned. No verified daily water/acreage.

gaps: Obtain current phase-specific power/occupancy, exact substantial-completion/first-service dates, final site plan, capex distinct from financing and parcel.

patch.title: Big Plain Solar:Operating 196 MW Plant; Operator Says Mid-2023, EIA September 2023
patch.description: LRE identifies Big Plain as a 196 MW solar project on approximately 1500 acres that began generating in mid-2023. EIA’s August 2026 operating inventory records plant 64635/GEN 01 at 196 MW with September 2023 operation. The prior 600 MW hybrid/$1.2 B/2028 story is removed.

references.title: Big Plain Solar — Leeward Renewable Energy
EIA860M — August2026 Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory
Big Plain Solar — Project Fact Sheet

patch.longFormSummary:
• The plant is solar; no separate storage capacity is established. The opened operator overview and factsheet publish no$1.2 B construction budget.
  • Map now follows EIA’s reported plant point 39.855658,-83.32843, consistent with the operator’s London/Big Plain vicinity map; it is not a surveyed property boundary.
  • Timeline: September 1,2023 is month-only precision from EIA. LRE’s mid-2023 wording may describe initial generation rather than the EIA commercial milestone; the difference remains explicit.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: EIA operating month September 2023; LRE says generation began mid-2023. Month precision, exact milestones unresolved.
patch.address: Near London and Big Plain, Madison County, Ohio, USA (EIA reported plant point)

power.note: Operating solar rating; no verified hybrid battery capacity.

gaps: Resolve initial-generation versus EIA operation month, exactCOD, capital budget and surveyed site boundary; do not infer a new600MW hybrid phase.

patch.title: Dolphin Solar Dequine–Eugene:250 MW Uprate to 700 MW Combined Output
patch.description: PJM’s June 2026 Phase II study identifies AG2-163, Dolphin Solar LLC, as a 250 MW solar uprate to AG1-226, taking combined maximum output to 700 MW. This is a linked interconnection development, not an independently permitted 700 MW facility with a published$1.3 B budget.

references.title: AG2-163 PhaseII System Impact Study Report

patch.longFormSummary:
• PJM lists MFO 700 MW, incremental energy 250 MW and incremental capacity 35 MW; combined recognized capacity 177 MW. These study quantities are distinct from storage or measured generation.
  • The study discusses a network upgrade estimated in-service June 2030, with interim deliverability study possible. That upgrade date is not a project COD guarantee.
  • Timeline: December 31,2029 remains an unverified legacy COD. Construction scope, developer schedule and final permits still require evidence.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy December 2029 COD; June 2030 upgrade dependency is not itself a project opening date.

power.note: Combined maximum facility output after 250 MW AG2-163 uprate to 450 MW AG1-226; not an independent 700 MW addition.

gaps: Verify current permits, site identity/parcel, developer COD, construction budget and interim deliverability; do not double count linked450+250MW requests.
